one_liner: .NET RPC library (Fusion's transport) that multiplexes calls over one WebSocket; vendor loopback benchmark shows 5-8x grpc-dotnet call throughput.
what_it_does: ActualLab.Rpc is the RPC layer of the Fusion real-time framework. You can use it without Fusion through the ActualLab.Rpc (client) and ActualLab.Rpc.Server (ASP.NET Core host) NuGet packages. You declare a plain C# interface that derives from IRpcService with Task-returning methods (no .proto files), implement it on the server, and get a source-generated client proxy that calls it over a persistent WebSocket (an HTTP/2 transport also exists). It adds server-to-client streaming (RpcStream<T>), reconnection, call routing and a TypeScript client, but it is not wire-compatible with gRPC, so it replaces gRPC only where you control both ends.
how_it_is_fast: All calls from one client peer share one WebSocket. The frame-based writer (RpcFrameBasedTransport) drains a channel of queued messages, serializes them back-to-back into a pooled buffer, and flushes a frame when it reaches FrameSize (12,000 bytes by default) or when the queue is empty. Under load, many calls therefore go out in one write (opportunistic write coalescing, with no timer by default), and the next frame is serialized while the previous one flushes. Each call is a compact binary envelope (varint call IDs) with MessagePack or MemoryPack arguments, and proxies are source-generated (ActualLab.Interception: 1 allocation per call, no boxing); RpcStream<T> sends items in batches of up to 1024 under an ack-window flow control, where gRPC sends one protobuf message per item.
when_to_use: Both ends are .NET (ASP.NET Core server; .NET, Blazor WebAssembly or MAUI clients), and you have many small unary calls where per-call overhead dominates. Sum/GetUser-sized payloads were 7-8x grpc-dotnet in the vendor localhost test.

Many concurrent callers share each connection. The writer batches whatever is queued into about 12 KB frames, so the gain grows with in-flight calls (the benchmark uses 200 concurrent tasks per client for calls).
Server streaming of small items (1-100 bytes each), for example telemetry or UI feeds. The vendor results were 1.7-2.3x gRPC on localhost and 2.1-3.0x in the 4-CPU Docker run.
A browser or TypeScript front end talks to a .NET back end and you would otherwise use gRPC-Web or SignalR. @actuallab/rpc uses the same wire format (json5np or msgpack6/msgpack6c).
You already use Fusion, or you plan to. Compute Service Clients add client-side caching with server-pushed invalidation on top of the same transport.
when_not_to_use: Polyglot systems. Only .NET and TypeScript implementations exist, contracts are C# interfaces, not .proto files, and gRPC clients, proxies and tooling cannot talk to it.
Large-payload streaming. The lead shrinks to 1.4x at 10 KB items on localhost (8.27 vs 5.86 GB/s) and to about 2x in Docker.

Workloads that care about single-call latency at low concurrency. The published latencies are measured at saturation, and in the 4-CPU Docker run gRPC had the lower p50 (SayHello 4.2 ms vs 6.4 ms; Sum 3.3 ms vs 3.5 ms), although ActualLab.Rpc had the lower p99 on Sum (12.8 ms vs 45.4 ms).
You need independent or Linux bare-metal numbers before you commit. All published results are the vendor's own, on Windows loopback and Docker Desktop/WSL2.
Payloads above 15.5 MiB per call, or older mixed-runtime clients that exchange interface-typed values. See gotchas.

integration.form: module: NuGet packages (ActualLab.Rpc for clients, ActualLab.Rpc.Server for ASP.NET Core hosting), with a Roslyn source generator (ActualLab.Generators)
integration.dependencies: ActualLab.Core, ActualLab.Interception, ActualLab.Generators (compile-time), MemoryPack (default serializer) or MessagePack-CSharp; System.IO.Pipelines package on pre-net9 targets; the server side needs ASP.NET Core
integration.min_toolchain: ActualLab.Rpc.csproj multi-targets netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, netcoreapp3.1 and net5.0-net10.0; the HTTP/2 client transport needs net5+. The benchmark ran on .NET 10.0.8.
integration.platforms: Any .NET runtime (server, Blazor WebAssembly, MAUI per README); Native AOT and trimming are supported (runtime codegen switches to interpreted expressions); TypeScript client via @actuallab/rpc
integration.thread_safety: Not documented as a statement. The benchmark shares one client proxy (one peer and WebSocket) across 200 concurrent tasks, which is the intended usage.

gotchas: Size limits (tightened in v14.2): a message whose argument data exceeds 15.5 MiB, or whose header or method reference exceeds 1 KiB, is dropped on receive with no error reply. The caller sees the call as never answered.

Abstract and interface-typed arguments and results are sent with a runtime type name (TypeRef). Open issue #60: a net472 client calling a net10 server that returns IList<string> fails with 'Type System.Collections.Generic.List`1[...], System.Private.CoreLib is not found'.

The format is chosen per connection (?f=key), and both peers must support it. The README says MemoryPack is the default and MessagePack (msgpack6c, used in the benchmark) needs runtime IL emit. The TypeScript client supports only JSON and MessagePack, with no MemoryPack and no polymorphism.

RpcStream defaults are BatchSize 64, AckPeriod 30 and AckAdvance 61. The benchmark server overrides them to BatchSize 200 for items under 50 bytes, AckPeriod 900 and AckAdvance 1801. Expect lower stream throughput without similar tuning.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: All other catalogued entries that beat gRPC are for Go (rpcx, Kitex, DRPC, cmd-stream, fRPC, Exposed), Rust (wtx) or C++ (brpc, grpcxx), so pick ActualLab.Rpc when both ends are .NET, or when a TypeScript client talks to a .NET server. Pick wtx or grpcxx instead if you must stay on the gRPC wire protocol.
verified_claims_summary: The vendor's harness (Fusion.Samples src/RpcBenchmark) runs the ASP.NET Core server and the clients in one process over TLS on 127.0.0.1, on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D with Windows 11 and .NET 10.0.8. Worker count and concurrency are auto-tuned for each framework, and the best of 6 x 5 s runs is reported. ActualLab.Rpc (msgpack6c over WebSocket) did 9.91M/8.75M/6.04M calls/s on Sum/GetUser/SayHello vs grpc-dotnet's 1.28M/1.24M/1.16M (5.2-7.7x), and 1.4-2.3x more stream items/s. With the server limited to 4 CPUs in Docker, SayHello ran at 2.52M vs 399.32K calls/s (~6.3x) and Sum at 4.77M vs 437.85K (~10.9x, derived).
status_note: Actively maintained: last commit 2026-09-15, about 5,500 commits, ActualLab.Rpc 14.4.16 on NuGet with ~663K total downloads. MIT-licensed and usable standalone from Fusion, but the published benchmarks were run on v14.0.17.
